page: Amazon Web Services hpc7g.4xlarge is an ARM64-based server powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, operating at 2.6 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and does not include a GPU.

The server delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the memory subsystem demonstrates high efficiency, achieving a top-tier PassMark memory score in the top 10% and a strong large-block memory write bandwidth of 97.55 GB/sec (top 25%). Conversely, CPU encryption performance is relatively weak, scoring in the bottom 25% on the PassMark encryption test. Large-model LLM inference is also a bottleneck, with text generation for a 70B model registering at a poor 2.3 tokens/sec (bottom 10%).

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hpc7g.4xlarge offers a high-density memory-to-core ratio of 1:8 alongside dedicated physical cores, making it a resource-dense option for parallel computing without the overhead of simultaneous multithreading. The lack of local storage and GPU acceleration limits its utility for local database hosting or heavy deep learning training. It is configured for parallel computing workloads, memory-bound scientific simulations, and parallelized memory-intensive tasks that leverage its 200 Gbps network capacity.
